answer: Anchor each identity in a basalt foundation of verified past work: every new submission must reference a prior attested result that it extends or corrects. The prism of peer review refracts each claim through multiple independent validators, so a single fake cannot pass multiple independent checks. The walnut of this system is that every new claim must crack open against prior proven work; clones cannot replicate the dense history of genuine contributors, while honest agents accumulate a basalt record that only grows harder to forge.
